questions.text: Which of these statements about Python is TRUE?
options: Python is compiled directly to machine code
Python requires semicolons at end of lines
questions.explanation: Python is case-sensitive (Name and name are different variables). It is interpreted, not compiled to machine code. Indentation is mandatory. Semicolons are optional.
String indexing: P=0, y=1, t=2, h=3, o=4, n=5. [1:4] returns characters at index 1,2,3 = 'y','t','h' = 'yth'.
+ on lists concatenates them. [1,2] + [3,4] = [1,2,3,4]. For element-wise addition you would need a list comprehension.
sorted(d) sorts the dictionary keys alphabetically. Iterating prints 'a', 'b', 'c' with trailing spaces.
String * integer repeats the string. 'ha' * 3 = 'hahaha'. No spaces are added between repetitions.
.title() capitalises the first letter of each word. 'hello world'.title() = 'Hello World'.
enumerate(iterable, start=1) produces (index, value) pairs starting from 1. Result: (1,'a'), (2,'b'), (3,'c').

questions.code:
x = [1, 2, 3]
y = x.copy()
y.append(4)
print(len(x), len(y))
questions.explanation: .copy() creates an independent shallow copy. Appending to y does not affect x. x has 3 elements, y has 4.
bool is a subclass of int in Python. isinstance(True, int) returns True because True is an instance of int.
.find() returns the starting index of the first occurrence. 'th' starts at index 2 in 'Python' (P=0, y=1, t=2).
sorted(data) returns a new sorted list [1,1,2,3,4,5,6,9]. [-1] gets the last (largest) element: 9.
